title: GPS-WQLOG: logarithmically corrected width attains time leading coefficient1/2 at the same source budget

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, n=ceil(log2 N), the single GPS-WQLOG algorithm/configuration of proof.md (finite branch n<2^32; otherwise r=ceil(sqrt n), ell=ceil(log2 n), z=ceil(log2 ell), b=r(ell+2z+9), m=ceil((n-1)/b), corrected constant-wide profile, above-half r_i=b_i+1 Grover combiner, original all-modulus decoders and exactly the acquisition and high-confidence-fallback cutoffs) recovers the full secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8>3/4 from independent ideal copies. On EVERY execution branch including retries, failed attempts, discarded copies and aborts, its total charged sequential work T(N,s) is O(2^((1/2)sqrt n*log2 n+2sqrt(n log2 n))). The exact uniform envelope B(n)=2^((1/2)sqrt n*log2 n+2sqrt(n log2 n)) has growth index1/2 with an absolute outside constant. The literal source-cap inequality holds on every main n>=2^32, and Section9 proves the time envelope for n>=2^1024 with finite-prefix absorption below it. All source, label, circuit generation, classical processing, decoder, initialization, reset, measurement and addressing costs are counted. This holds jointly with the other resource and zero-tolerance claims for this same two-cutoff algorithm.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single GPS-WQLOG algorithm and complete parameter rule of proof.md (constant-wide source-budget profile of Section4.1, Grover pair search, acquisition cutoff Qcap and capped verified-extraction fallback Cf; no weighted-attempt cutoff) recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8 > 3/4 from independent ideal source copies. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, discarded copies, failed attempts and aborts, its peak allocated classical bits obey S_C(N,s) = O(n^2). The uniform bit-length envelope is B_C(n) = n^2 for n >= 2, with the explicit finite branch covering all smaller cases. Its exact growth index is 0. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes, and this bound holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the zero-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single GPS-WQLOG algorithm and complete parameter rule of proof.md (constant-wide source-budget profile of Section4.1, Grover pair search, acquisition cutoff Qcap and capped verified-extraction fallback Cf; no weighted-attempt cutoff) recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8 > 3/4 from independent ideal source copies. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, discarded copies, failed attempts and aborts, its peak allocated qubits obey S_Q(N,s) = O(n). The uniform bit-length envelope is B_Q(n) = n for n >= 2, with the explicit finite branch covering all smaller cases. Its exact growth index is 0. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes, and this bound holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the zero-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, n=ceil(log2 N), the single GPS-WQLOG algorithm/configuration of proof.md (finite branch n<2^32; otherwise r=ceil(sqrt n), ell=ceil(log2 n), z=ceil(log2 ell), b=r(ell+2z+9), m=ceil((n-1)/b), corrected constant-wide profile, above-half r_i=b_i+1 Grover combiner, original all-modulus decoders and exactly the acquisition and high-confidence-fallback cutoffs) recovers the full secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8>3/4 from independent ideal copies. On EVERY execution branch including retries, failed attempts, discarded copies and aborts, its total number Q(N,s) of fresh source copies acquired, including every rejected, failed and discarded copy is O(2^((1/2)sqrt n)). The exact uniform envelope B(n)=2^((1/2)sqrt n) has growth index1/2 with an absolute outside constant. The literal source-cap inequality holds on every main n>=2^32, and Section9 proves the time envelope for n>=2^1024 with finite-prefix absorption below it. All source, label, circuit generation, classical processing, decoder, initialization, reset, measurement and addressing costs are counted. This holds jointly with the other resource and zero-tolerance claims for this same two-cutoff algorithm.

For the same GPS-WQLOG algorithm and complete parameter rule in proof.md, the proved malformed-sample fractional guarantee is epsilon(n)=0: all Q acquired source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, unconditional full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1-2^-8 > 3/4 jointly with all four every-branch resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted, and this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
